title: The Reformed grant inward helps to the unconverted
source_text: LXXIV. Ultro etiam concedunt, illis ipsis qui Evangelium audientes non convertuntur, neque peccato renunciant, praeter externam praedicationis gratiam, multa interna gratiae auxilia communicari, Deumque variis modis intus cor eorum pulsare, & mentem illustrare, ut a peccato recedant, & eam quam par est fidem Evangelio adhibeant: ita ut propria tantum culpa pereant, & per solam eorum perversitatem & contumaciam stet, quin salutis fiant participes.
pass_a_gloss: LXXIV. They also grant freely, that to those very people who hearing the Gospel are not converted, nor renounce sin, besides the external grace of preaching, many internal helps of grace are communicated, & that God in various ways knocks inwardly at their heart, & illuminates the mind, that they may withdraw from sin, & give to the Gospel the faith which is due: so that they perish only by their own fault, & it is only through their perversity & obstinacy that they do not become partakers of salvation.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXXIV. They also freely grant that those who hear the Gospel and are not converted or do not give up sin receive, besides the outward grace of preaching, many inward helps of grace. God knocks at their hearts from within in various ways and enlightens their minds, so that they may turn from sin and give the Gospel the faith it deserves.
So they perish only through their own fault, and it is their perversity and obstinacy alone that keeps them from sharing in salvation.
